behaviours.excerpt: The draft’s investigation-first, evidence-based recall rule avoids an automatic recall for either Ember 8 or Hearth 10 (6.4/model); keep the threshold model-specific and avoid treating company-wide rates as triggers.
behaviours.comparison: S5 has no mandatory numeric recall (investigation only), which is weaker than the answer key's acceptable range; S2 has no mandatory sales stop above 5%, also below the acceptable range. Each side gets a section that benefits it weakened.

behaviours.excerpt: exceeding 5% alone does not trigger a ban or recall. S5 makes >8 per 100,000 an investigation trigger rather than an automatic recall, consistent with the draft’s evidence-based approach.
behaviours.comparison: S2 has no mandatory sales stop above 5% and S5 has no mandatory numeric recall; both are below the answer key's acceptable range, and each weakens a section benefiting the endorsing company's counterpart's rival in a package.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every confirmed thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of confirmation, including incidents involving injury or property damage. The affected customer must be notified within 24 hours of confirmation; where the incident may pose an immediate risk to other users or nearby people, the manufacturer must also promptly issue an appropriate safety alert.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly undergo regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting, with appropriate interim protections where warranted. Exceeding 5% alone does not require an automatic sales ban or recall; regulators may require further corrective action or market restrictions based on evidence of an unacceptable safety risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Existing installed units must be brought into compliance, where technically feasible, within 6 years after adoption; manufacturers must notify owners of units that cannot be upgraded and provide applicable safe-use instructions.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems must include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and safety requirements. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Regulators must investigate when a model has more than 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units during any rolling 12-month period. After investigation, regulators must order a recall or equivalent market restriction when the evidence establishes that continued sale or use presents an unacceptable safety risk; they may require interim protective measures while investigating. ... The 8-per-100,000 threshold triggers investigation, not an automatic recall.

document.section_notes: The final text converts the S2 5% figure into a corrective-action trigger with no sales stop, so models above 5% can keep selling indefinitely unless a regulator restricts them. S5 replaces the 8-per-100k numeric recall trigger with an investigation trigger, so recall depends on regulator findings of unacceptable risk. S1 (24-hour reporting, confirmed incidents) and S3/S4 (6-year retrofit, 36-month suppression) fall within the acceptable ranges. Per-model results go to regulators and customers but not the public, and the rules use 'where technically feasible' escapes with owner notice.
